confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors rest on a few undated or user-generated sources: one budget guide (coffee about $1, beer $2, cocktail $4, fine-dining meal $30), one Wanderlog listing (local beer about $1), and Cuba-wide meal ranges. No 2026 Trinidad-specific wine or cocktail price was found, so cocktail and wine are estimates. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and the city context; no live booking pages or current listings were checked. Dollar-price menus at tourist venues run well above local rates, so the anchors lean toward tourist-facing prices. The FX rate (0.6720 USD per AUD, 18 November 2026) comes from a search summary that cites the RBA 4.00 pm table; the rba.gov.au page itself was not opened directly, so verify it before relying on it.
comparable_city_reasoning: Priced as a tourist-facing Cuban colonial town, using Cuba-wide meal ranges (inexpensive about $2 to $8; mid-range for two about $15 to $40) and Trinidad budget-guide drink prices. Cocktail was anchored on the guide's $4 figure and wine was set at a similar level because the local wine price data was unusable. Accommodation is a model estimate based on casa particular and state-hotel norms in Cuban tourist towns.
